newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to easier.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to easier.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended steady to easier in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Wednesday.

"The interbank rate eased slightly again today but still had little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were quietly steady but bond prices were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months was unchanged from Tuesday's yield of 0.85/0.80 percent and one-year unchanged from Tuesday's yield of 1.55/1.50 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.99/99.04 compared with Tuesday's close of S$99.00/99.05, September 2001 at S$97.30/97.35 against S$97.35/97.40 and June 2003 at S$95.30/95.35 from S$95.37/95.42.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 3 2-7/8 percent versus Tuesday's 3-1/8 3 percent.
